dc.identifier.next_section.value: 8.Speaker or Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) Every Legislative Assembly shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the Assembly to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker thereof and, so often as the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant, the Assembly shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be.
(2) A member holding office as Speaker or Deputy Speaker of an Assembly—
(a) shall vacate his office if he ceases to be a member of the Assembly;
(b) may at any time by writing under his hand addressed, if such member is the Speaker, to the Deputy Speaker, and if such member is the Deputy Speaker, to the Speaker, resign his office;

(3) While the office of Speaker is vacant, the duties of the office shall be performed by the Deputy Speaker or, if the office of Deputy Speaker is also vacant, by such member of the Assembly as may be determined by the rules of procedure of the Assembly.
(4) During the absence of the Speaker from any sitting of the Assembly, the Deputy Speaker, or, if he is also absent, such person as may be determined by the rules of procedure of the Assembly, or, if no such person is present, such other person as may be determined by the Assembly, shall act as Speaker.
(5) There shall be paid to the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly such salaries and allowances as may be respectively fixed by the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries and allowances as the Administrator may, with the approval of the President, by order determine.

indexableObject.name: Discharge of surety of creditor's act or omission impairing surety's eventual remedy.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
If the creditor does any act which is inconsistent with the rights of the surety, or omits to do any act which his duty to the surety requires him to do, and the eventual remedy of the surety himself against the principal debtor is thereby impaired, the surety is discharged.
Illustrations
(a) B contracts to build a ship for C for a given sum, to be paid by instalments as the work reaches certain stages. A becomes surety to C for B's due performance of the contract. C, without the knowledge of A, prepays to B the last two instalments. A is discharged by this prepayment.
(b) C lends money to B on the security of a joint and several promissory note made in C's favour by B, and by A as surety for B, together with a bill of sale of B's furniture, which gives power to C to sell the furniture, and apply the proceeds in discharge of the note. Subsequently, C sells the furniture, but, owing to his misconduct and wilful negligence, only a small price is realized. A is discharged from liability on the note.
(c) A puts M as apprentice to B, and gives a guarantee to B for M's fidelity. B promises on his part that he will, at least once a month, see M make up the cash. B omits to see this done as promised, and M embezzles. A is not liable to B on his guarantee.

dc.description.abstract.value:
summary of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975
Objective
The Customs Tariff Act, 1975 was enacted to consolidate and amend the law relating to customs duties. It provides the legal framework for levying customs duties on imported and exported goods, classifying goods under tariff schedules, and imposing additional, anti-dumping, countervailing, safeguard, and protective duties to protect domestic industry and regulate international trade. 
Key Provisions
•	Tariff Schedules: Prescribes the rates of import and export duties through the First Schedule (import tariff) and Second Schedule (export tariff). 
•	Additional Customs Duty: Provides for the levy of additional duty on imported goods equivalent to the excise duty or other applicable domestic taxes on similar goods produced in India. 
•	Preferential Tariff: Enables the application of preferential or lower rates of customs duty under trade agreements entered into by India. 
•	Protective and Emergency Duties: Empowers the Central Government to impose protective duties, increase import or export duties in emergencies, and modify tariff rates in the public interest. 
•	Anti-Dumping and Countervailing Duties: Authorises the levy of anti-dumping duties on dumped imports and countervailing duties on subsidised imported goods to protect domestic industries from unfair trade practices. 
•	Safeguard Measures: Provides for the imposition of safeguard duties where a surge in imports causes or threatens serious injury to domestic producers. 
•	Rule-making Power: Empowers the Central Government to amend tariff schedules in specified circumstances and make rules for implementing the provisions of the Act.

Summary of The Goa, Daman and Diu Mining Concession (Abolition and Declaration as Mining Leases) Act, 1987
Overview
1.	Objective: - Abolish mining concessions in Goa, Daman, and Diu under former Portuguese laws.
•	Convert these concessions into mining leases governed by the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957.
2.	Key Provisions: - Conversion Process:
•	First Schedule Concessions: Abolished from the "appointed day" (20th December 1961) and converted to mining leases.
•	Second Schedule Concessions: Abolished from the day after their grant date and converted similarly.
•	Lease Terms:
•	Initial Period: Up to 6 months from the Act's assent date.
•	Renewal: Subject to application and compliance with the Mines and Minerals Act, 1957.
3.	Definitions & Precedence:
•	"Appointed Day": Defined as 20th December 1961.
•	Precedence: This Act overrides any conflicting laws, court orders, or judgments.

An Act to provide for the abolition of the mining concessions in operation in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu and specified in the First and the Second Schedules, and for the declaration of such mining concessions as mining leases under the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 with a view to the regulation of the mines to which such concessions relate and for the development of minerals under the control of the Union and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

AND WHEREAS it is expedient in the public interest to abolish such mining concessions and declare them as mining leases under the aforesaid Act for the purpose of making the provisions of that Act applicable to the mines to which such concessions relate with a view to the regulation of such mines and for the development of minerals under the control of the Union so as to subserve the common good:
BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Republic of India as follows:--

(1) The appropriate Government shall ensure that—
(a) there is a legitimate and bona fide public purpose for the proposed acquisition which necessitates the acquisition of the land identified;
(b) the potential benefits and the public purpose referred to in clause (a) shall outweigh the social costs and adverse social impact as determined by the Social Impact Assessment that has been carried out;
(c) only the minimum area of land required for the project is proposed to be acquired;
(d) there is no unutilised land which has been previously acquired in the area;
(e) the land, if any, acquired earlier and remained unutilised, is used for such public purpose and make recommendations in respect thereof.
(2) The appropriate Government shall examine the report of the Collector, if any, and the report of the Expert Group on the Social Impact Assessment study and after considering all the reports, recommend such area for acquisition which would ensure minimum displacement of people, minimum disturbance to the infrastructure, ecology and minimum adverse impact on the individuals affected.

Provided that where land is sought to be acquired for the purposes as specified in sub-section (2) of section 2, the appropriate Government shall also ascertain as to whether the prior consent of the affected families as required under the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 2, has been obtained in the manner as may be prescribed.
